faq.a: Abdulhalim represents Arabic عَبْدُ الْحَلِيم, meaning servant of the Forbearing.

faq.q: What is the origin of Abdulhalim?
faq.a: The name is Arabic and is a compound of عبد and a second element.
Yes. The underlying compound is عَبْدُ الْحَلِيم (ʿAbd al-Ḥalīm).

faq.q: What is the root of Abdulhalim?
faq.a: عبد is related to ع ب د; al-Ḥalīm is related to ح ل م (ḥ-l-m).
Abdulhalim is a traditional Muslim personal name because it contains a compound invoking al-Ḥalīm, a divine epithet in Islamic tradition.
This record does not establish Abdulhalim as an explicitly named Qur'anic person; the compound's religious meaning is distinct from personal-name attestation in the text.

faq.q: What does Abdulhalim mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, the name means servant of the Forbearing; the compound combines عبد with al-Ḥalīm.
The supplied “ab-dul-ha-lim” is an approximate pronunciation; local pronunciations vary.

faq.q: Is Abdulhalim a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: The record classifies the name as masculine, consistent with traditional usage; regional frequency data is not supplied.
